title: Quickswitch kernel handoff scratch
content:
Context:
- Midweek spike: p99 token latency increased ~150ms on model-web-rt (gpt-small-ish) around 2026-02-28 09:40 UTC.
- Likely correlated with recent micro-batching change + new KV prefetch heuristic (PR 2094).
- Oncall asked for a short handoff; this is the scratchpad for whoever picks this up.

What I saw (quick):
- Canary metrics: throughput stable, p50 unchanged, p95 +30ms, p99 +150ms.
- Telemetry: increased time in "kv-cache-lookup" span and higher syscalls/sec on one host pool (dc-us-west-2-a).
- Rolling deploy: partial rollout of batch-size tuning (auto-batch v2) started 2026-02-28 08:50 and hit ~20% traffic.

Open hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV prefetch/adaptive eviction causing occasional blocking on cache miss path that holds a lock during async prefetch.
2) Batch scheduler change introduced head-of-line blocking for long sequences when autoscaling interacts with batching windows.
3) NUMA/cuda pinning issue on one host causing occasional GPU stall during KV fetch kernel launch.

Immediate triage checklist (do in order):
- [ ] Pull logs for INF-7123 window (09:35-09:50) from dc-us-west-2-a hosts (hostnames: rwi-*-usw2-a).
- [ ] Check span breakdown for affected requests: kv-cache-lookup, batch-assemble, kernel-launch. Use tracing ui or `otel query` quick query.
- [ ] Rollback autoscale/batch-v2 to previous config for 1 host pool (canary) if reproducible locally.
- [ ] If rollback reduces p99 in canary, escalate and stop rollout.

Useful commands (notes to self):
- Fetch logs: gcloud compute ssh --project redwood-prod --zone us-west2-a rwi-123 -- 'sudo journalctl -u rwi-service --since "2026-02-28 09:30" --until "2026-02-28 09:55" > /tmp/inf-7123.log'
- Tracing span view: open https://tracing.redwood.ai/query?trace=INF-7123 (replace with trace id), or use otel-cli to pull traces for trace.status=error
- Hotpath perf: sudo perf record -F 200 -g -p $(pgrep rwi-runtime) -- sleep 20; sudo perf report --call-graph
- Kernel / nvprof: /opt/cuda/bin/nvprof --profile-child-processes --output-profile /tmp/nvprof.pf -- /usr/bin/rwi-runtime --mode test

Quick manual repro steps (dev env):
1) Checkout PR 2094 locally (github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2094).
2) Start local runtime with small batch window: ./rwi-runtime --batch-window-ms=8 --kv-prefetch=on --kv-prefetch-threads=2
3) Run load generator (scripts/load-local.sh --model gpt-small-ish --seq-len 1024 --qps 60) and watch for 95/99 latency regressions.

Small experiments to run (short):
- A: Disable kv-prefetch for 2 minutes in canary (config flag) -> observe p99. If improves, dig into cache lock paths.
- B: Change batch-window-ms from 8 -> 4 on one canary host to see head-of-line effect.
- C: Force single-job GPU affinity (NUMA pin) to confirm kernel stall hypothesis.

Notes on KV cache internals:
- Prefetch kicks in when request token prefix length > 64 and predicted next-block == remote.
- Prefetch uses background thread pool; it holds an insertion lock briefly and enqueues IO. If prefetch IO stalls, some callers may wait on 'wait_for_prefetch' with timeout = 120ms.
- Recent change (PR 2094) adjusts backpressure and increases prefetch concurrency; might increase lock contention.

Handoff items for the next person:
- If you take this: start by running repro locally (Quick steps above). Send me a short slack with findings before doing any service-level rollback.
- If rolling back, use rollout policy doc: Confluence -> "deploy/runbook/rolling-config-revert" (shortcut: confluence:rolling-revert).
- If you need more telemetry, enable DEBUG spans for kv-cache for 5m only: POST /admin/flags {"span.debug.kv":true} then collect traces.

Questions I'm leaving unresolved (decide during triage):
- Is the prefetch lock too coarse? Consider switching to per-shard locks if contention visible.
- Should wait_for_prefetch be converted to a nonblocking best-effort path with fallback to remote fetch in critical-latency path?
- Is there correlation with a specific customer workload (long prompts) or is it general?

Handoff checklist for oncall (short):
- Slack channel: #rwi-runtime (ping @ivy @noor).
- Pager duty: INF-runtime-rotation (if paging threshold > 3s).
- If p99 > 400ms AND errors spike -> perform canary rollback of PR 2094 (see rollback steps).

Todo (me / follow ups):
- [ ] Add microbenchmark for kv-insert lock overhead with concurrency 1..32 (write bench in c++ harness).
- [ ] Add span metrics for prefetch queue wait time (histogram).
- [ ] Create follow-up ticket to investigate per-shard locks + nonblocking prefetch fallback (tentative: INF-7189).
- [ ] Update PR 2094 with optional prefetch disabled flag and default off for next rollout.

Reference links / artifacts:
- JIRA: JIRA-INF-7123 (latency spike investigation)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2094
- Confluence draft: confluence:kv-cache-eviction-draft

Random quick notes / brain dump:
- If prefetch thread pool is oversubscribed, it may queue on OS thread creation; consider using a fixed thread pool pinned to a CPU set.
- Potential short-term mitigation: add fail-fast to prefetch after X ms and let main path fetch directly (worse cost, better latency).
- Remember this saw location-specific concentration (us-west-2-a) -> could be infra/placement or machine image. Check AMI version differences.

End of scratch - pick this up next shift.

— Gideon
